newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman says will heed Arab decisions on Israel ties.
newsitem.headline: Oman says will heed Arab decisions on Israel ties.

text.p: An Omani minister said on Monday his country would follow any Arab decision on relations with Israel, but did not say whether Oman would shut down Israel's trade office in Muscat.

Oman's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah spoke on his return from an Arab foreign ministers meeting in Cairo. The ministers recommended that Arab states put an end to normal relations with Israel and restore the old economic boycott of the Jewish state.
"The Sultanate is committed to any decision taken by the Arab states," he said, as quoted by the official Oman News Agency.
The ministers, at the end of a two-day meeting, said they would also close down Israeli missions and withdraw from multilateral talks on Middle East peace.

Oman has forged ahead with establishing economic ties with Israel after the Israeli-Palestinian 1993 peace accord. Last August it became the first Gulf Arab country to have any representation in Israel after opening a commercial bureau in Tel Aviv. Israel has also set up a similar office in Muscat.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies have put a damper on Muscat's enthusiasm and it has recently joined a chorus of condemnation of Israel by the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
On March 23, Oman said it had frozen ties with Israel over the Jewish state's settlement policies.
At the Arab League meeting, Alawi said his country would "most probably" close the representative office in Israel "when necessary".
The minister would not be drawn on the issue upon his return to Muscat.
